Kubbly helps brands become a verified contact on customers’ phones. Customers text the brand like they text a friend. Your brand's AI agent, powered by Kubbly, autonomously understands your customer, remembers context, and maintains conversation memory to serve them better every time, from intent to secure checkout.

We are laser-focused on helping brands use this channel aligned with your customer's needs to build long-term relationships, prioritizing trust over short-term wins. It behaves like a friend you would trust in iMessage or WhatsApp.Kubbly turns the message thread into a branded, interactive experience. Your customers browse, decide, and complete checkout inside the conversation. They stay in one place from intent to action.

We build the infrastructure that makes this work at scale. We verify identity and protect access. We preserve context across sessions so the experience improves over time. We enforce guardrails so the agent stays on brand and acts safely.

Brands use Kubbly to remove steps between intent and completion. They increase conversion because customers do not leave the inbox. You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

Customer Experience is no longer about surveys. It’s about signals.

What are the consequences for a company if it knows a customer is dissatisfied even before the customer complains or realizes their dissatisfaction?

With CQI, you can detect and act on customer dissatisfaction before it turns into a complaint, churn, or lost revenue - thanks to real-time AI-driven signals.

CQI is an AI-powered Customer Experience (CX) and Customer Intelligence platform that helps enterprises understand, measure, and improve customer relationships in real time and at scale.

At the core of CQI is Verified CX - a new approach to CX management that goes beyond traditional NPS and point-in-time feedback. The platform unifies conversational intelligence, customer feedback, behavioral data, and operational events into a single, continuously updated metric: the Customer Quality Index (CQI).

CQI provides an AI-driven score that reflects each customer’s true relationship health across the entire customer lifecycle. Powered by advanced AI and predictive analytics, CQI continuously learns from every interaction, correlates experience signals with operational data, and surfaces early friction, churn risk, and growth opportunities - often before customers complain or disengage.

CQI goes beyond insight delivery. The platform activates intelligence by triggering targeted interventions, personalized engagement, and automated actions across sales, service, and operations. This enables organizations to reduce churn, increase retention, drive upsell and cross-sell, and improve customer satisfaction, all based on trusted, real-time data.

Whether the objective is maximizing customer lifetime value (CLV), reducing operational costs, or building long-term customer loyalty, CQI transforms complex, fragmented data into clear, actionable intelligence - helping teams anticipate customer needs, resolve issues proactively, and drive sustainable business growth.

entity.name: Converso
entity.description:
Converso is an AI-native customer support platform built for modern SaaS teams.
As SaaS products scale, customer expectations rise faster than support teams can grow. Support leaders are under pressure to deliver instant, high-quality answers across every channel, whilst keeping costs down and avoiding bloated, inflexible helpdesk tools.

Converso helps SaaS companies do more with less by combining AI agents and human support in one intelligent system. Our AI assistants resolve common questions instantly across web chat and WhatsApp, drawing on structured, AI-readable business knowledge to give accurate, on-brand answers. When a conversation needs a person, Converso hands off seamlessly and in context - so customers never lose the thread and your team stays focused on the cases that matter.

Unlike traditional support tools, Converso is built for continuous AI–human collaboration, not disconnected bot-and-ticket workflows. The result: higher deflection, faster resolution, and better customer experiences, without sacrificing control or trust.

You also get a shared omnichannel inbox, GDPR-compliant conversation history, customer context that follows people across channels, and built-in tools to capture leads and follow up on sales or onboarding enquiries.

And we're building for what's next. Increasingly, it won't just be customers reaching out, it'll be the personal AI agents acting on their behalf. Converso is built to receive them, so your business is ready for AI-driven conversations as they arrive, not scrambling to catch up.

Whether you're replacing an expensive helpdesk or adding AI to an existing support operation, Converso is a simpler, more cost-effective way for SaaS teams to scale support.

AI-powered support. Human when it matters. Ready for agents.

The messaging inbox is becoming the most valuable real estate on the phone. People live inside messaging apps. Brands want to meet customers there, but current tools make it difficult to engage in ways that feel helpful, branded, and trustworthy.

Most SMS marketing feels like spam. It comes from a random phone number or a 5-digit code. It contains random URLs that opens some page, force logins, or push app downloads. What should be the most personal, highest-conversion channel instead creates frustration, annoyance, and lost trust.

Kubbly helps brands become a verified contact on customers’ phones. Customers text the brand like they text a friend. Your brand's AI agent, powered by Kubbly, autonomously understands your customer, remembers context, and maintains conversation memory to serve them better every time, from intent to secure checkout.

We are laser-focused on helping brands use this channel aligned with your customer's needs to build long-term relationships, prioritizing trust over short-term wins. It behaves like a friend you would trust in iMessage or WhatsApp.Kubbly turns the message thread into a branded, interactive experience. Your customers browse, decide, and complete checkout inside the conversation. They stay in one place from intent to action.

We build the infrastructure that makes this work at scale. We verify identity and protect access. We preserve context across sessions so the experience improves over time. We enforce guardrails so the agent stays on brand and acts safely.

Brands use Kubbly to remove steps between intent and completion. They increase conversion because customers do not leave the inbox. They improve marketing ROI because each message completes a task, not just drives a click. They grow customer lifetime value because when you are in your buyers messaging apps, you are in their consideration set that much more often and that much more visible to them.

entity.name: Proponent
entity.description:
Proponent is a conversational-intelligence platform that helps Product Marketing, Sales and GTM teams understand their customers at scale.
Modern revenue teams generate thousands of conversations every month — sales calls, onboarding sessions, customer interviews, support interactions. Most of this rich customer context is never captured, analysed or shared in a structured way. Proponent changes that.

Our platform analyses customer conversations to identify:
• Pain points and unmet needs
• Objections and risks across deals
• Product references and feature requests
• Competitor mentions and market signals
• Trends in customer sentiment and language

Proponent transforms raw transcripts into organised, actionable insights that support core GTM workflows. Product Marketing teams use Proponent to refine messaging, validate ICP assumptions and develop narratives grounded in customer language. Sales and revenue teams use it to understand objection patterns, improve talk tracks and strengthen deal execution. Product and CX teams use the insights to detect friction points, uncover product gaps and prioritise improvements.

We integrate seamlessly with CRMs, call-recording platforms and support tools, enabling teams to analyse their existing conversation data without changing how they work. AI-powered summaries, weekly digest reports, trend detection and an interactive AI chat interface make insights easy to find and share across the organisation. Unlimited-user access ensures everyone works from the same customer truth.

Our mission is to help companies operate with a consistently customer-informed go-to-market strategy — using real language, real signals and real conversations.
Proponent enables teams to make clearer decisions, move faster and stay aligned as they scale.

entity.name: CQI Sense
entity.description:
Customer Experience is no longer about surveys. It’s about signals.

What are the consequences for a company if it knows a customer is dissatisfied even before the customer complains or realizes their dissatisfaction?

With CQI, you can detect and act on customer dissatisfaction before it turns into a complaint, churn, or lost revenue - thanks to real-time AI-driven signals.

CQI is an AI-powered Customer Experience (CX) and Customer Intelligence platform that helps enterprises understand, measure, and improve customer relationships in real time and at scale.

At the core of CQI is Verified CX - a new approach to CX management that goes beyond traditional NPS and point-in-time feedback. The platform unifies conversational intelligence, customer feedback, behavioral data, and operational events into a single, continuously updated metric: the Customer Quality Index (CQI).

CQI provides an AI-driven score that reflects each customer’s true relationship health across the entire customer lifecycle. Powered by advanced AI and predictive analytics, CQI continuously learns from every interaction, correlates experience signals with operational data, and surfaces early friction, churn risk, and growth opportunities - often before customers complain or disengage.

CQI goes beyond insight delivery. The platform activates intelligence by triggering targeted interventions, personalized engagement, and automated actions across sales, service, and operations. This enables organizations to reduce churn, increase retention, drive upsell and cross-sell, and improve customer satisfaction, all based on trusted, real-time data.

Whether the objective is maximizing customer lifetime value (CLV), reducing operational costs, or building long-term customer loyalty, CQI transforms complex, fragmented data into clear, actionable intelligence - helping teams anticipate customer needs, resolve issues proactively, and drive sustainable business growth.

#AI #VerifiedCX #ChurnPrevention

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.

  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.

  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.

  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

# Cogent Equity

Cogent Equity is a Investment Banking company. Cogent Equity helps owners of exceptional businesses navigate the sale process with clarity and firsthand experience. Their focus includes market positioning, operations, customer relationships, reputation, and growth potential, factors that build buyer confidence and increase sale price. Cogent Equity employs 2 people (+50.0% YoY, +1 person), founded in 2001. Headquartered in Seattle, Washington, United States.

## A

properties.name: Cogent Equity
properties.description:
Most transaction risk isn’t created during a sale process - it’s exposed by it.
 
By the time a business goes to market, many of the factors that determine value and deal certainty are already in place. We work with business owners and their advisors to evaluate those factors before the market does.
 
At Cogent Equity, we represent a limited number of companies with $1M to $10M in adjusted EBITDA, typically with long operating histories and strong underlying performance. Our focus is not just on running a process, but on ensuring the business is positioned to succeed in one.
 
This work often begins before a sale is imminent. We evaluate the business the way a sophisticated buyer would - identifying value constraints, aligning expectations, and addressing issues that would otherwise surface during diligence.
 
For advisors, the situations where it tends to be most useful to involve us are:
 
 - An owner is beginning to consider a sale in the next 1–3 years 
 - Valuation expectations are unclear or misaligned 
 - There are known or suspected issues that could impact a transaction 
 
Our perspective is shaped by firsthand experience as owners , operators, buyers, and sellers across nine different industries - allowing me to evaluate businesses the way a sophisticated buyer actually would.
 
While much of our work begins before a sale, we also represent owners through a structured, buyer-focused transaction process when the timing is right.
 
The objective is not just the right deal, but the right buyer - and a process that holds together from start to finish.

entity.name: Kubbly
entity.description:
The messaging inbox is becoming the most valuable real estate on the phone. People live inside messaging apps. Brands want to meet customers there, but current tools make it difficult to engage in ways that feel helpful, branded, and trustworthy.

Most SMS marketing feels like spam. It comes from a random phone number or a 5-digit code. It contains random URLs that opens some page, force logins, or push app downloads. What should be the most personal, highest-conversion channel instead creates frustration, annoyance, and lost trust.

Kubbly helps brands become a verified contact on customers’ phones. Customers text the brand like they text a friend. Your brand's AI agent, powered by Kubbly, autonomously understands your customer, remembers context, and maintains conversation memory to serve them better every time, from intent to secure checkout.

We are laser-focused on helping brands use this channel aligned with your customer's needs to build long-term relationships, prioritizing trust over short-term wins. It behaves like a friend you would trust in iMessage or WhatsApp.Kubbly turns the message thread into a branded, interactive experience. Your customers browse, decide, and complete checkout inside the conversation. They stay in one place from intent to action.

We build the infrastructure that makes this work at scale. We verify identity and protect access. We preserve context across sessions so the experience improves over time. We enforce guardrails so the agent stays on brand and acts safely.

Brands use Kubbly to remove steps between intent and completion. They increase conversion because customers do not leave the inbox. They improve marketing ROI because each message completes a task, not just drives a click. They grow customer lifetime value because when you are in your buyers messaging apps, you are in their consideration set that much more often and that much more visible to them.

Most transaction risk isn’t created during a sale process - it’s exposed by it.
 
By the time a business goes to market, many of the factors that determine value and deal certainty are already in place. We work with business owners and their advisors to evaluate those factors before the market does.
 
At Cogent Equity, we represent a limited number of companies with $1M to $10M in adjusted EBITDA, typically with long operating histories and strong underlying performance. Our focus is not just on running a process, but on ensuring the business is positioned to succeed in one.
 
This work often begins before a sale is imminent. We evaluate the business the way a sophisticated buyer would - identifying value constraints, aligning expectations, and addressing issues that would otherwise surface during diligence.
 
For advisors, the situations where it tends to be most useful to involve us are:
 
 - An owner is beginning to consider a sale in the next 1–3 years 
 - Valuation expectations are unclear or misaligned 
 - There are known or suspected issues that could impact a transaction 
 
Our perspective is shaped by firsthand experience as owners , operators, buyers, and sellers across nine different industries - allowing me to evaluate businesses the way a sophisticated buyer actually would.
 
While much of our work begins before a sale, we also represent owners through a structured, buyer-focused transaction process when the timing is right.
 
The objective is not just the right deal, but the right buyer - and a process that holds together from start to finish.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).

    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.

    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.
